A1.justification: Despite the changed title and organization, both PDFs describe the same IndoorTraj and camera-selection research, with matching authors, components, and experiments. Both complete documents, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original 3DGS and iNGP experiments on Replica and IndoorTraj, including rendering results, component ablations, and efficiency analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original synthetic-scene experiments and adds real-world evaluations on Mip-NeRF 360 and ScanNet, DPP comparisons, and hyperparameter analyses.

M1.justification: v2 adds a DPP/log-determinant selection alternative alongside the retained max-min approach. The documented factor-selection procedure changes from ILD/Kendall-tau balancing to empirical PSNR grid search. The spatial, angular, and semantic components remain; renaming ImgSim to DistSem is not itself a method change.

E1.justification: v2 retains Replica and IndoorTraj and adds actual evaluations on four indoor Mip-NeRF 360 scenes and four ScanNet scenes in Table 3. This substantially extends coverage from synthetic evaluations to real-world captures.

E2.justification: DPP becomes an evaluated alternative in the main comparisons and qualitative and sampling-ratio analyses. The existing Kopanas baseline, renamed zCF, is added to the ratio sweep where v1 explicitly excluded it. Random and Uniform also enter the timing comparison; zCF's renaming alone is not a new baseline.

E3.justification: The main 30,000-iteration, 5% synthetic-scene protocol and rendering backbones remain. New Mip-NeRF 360 evaluations use 20% of views, while ScanNet uses 5%. Reported metrics narrow to PSNR, and Appendix A changes living-1's training count from 2684 to 2632 without establishing whether this reflects resampling or correction.

E4.justification: v2 expands the openplan-1 case study and sampling-ratio analysis to examine competing utilities and numerical failures. PSNR grid-search heatmaps replace the ILD–PSNR association analysis. Equal-weight ablations and the joint training-time/sample-size efficiency study disappear, while the other component ablations remain.

E5.justification: v1's Kendall-tau association estimation and validation between ILD and PSNR are removed. Uncertainty reporting otherwise retains means and standard deviations over five sampling seeds, without an explicit increase in runs or new confidence-interval or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: v2 adds DPP scores and eight real-scene PSNR comparisons while retaining the original main-table means. The 3DGS living-1 standard deviation changes from 0.12 to 0.32. SSIM/LPIPS and joint resource-efficiency results disappear. Reported coverage-sampler times change from 1149.6/2445.4 seconds to 239/325 seconds for Replica/IndoorTraj, without enough explanation to establish a comparable speedup.

T1.justification: Sections 3–4 add formal definitions of submodularity, monotonicity, and utility-function domains; propositions and proof arguments for DPP and max-min utilities; a coverage-function derivation; and discussion of greedy approximation guarantees. This substantially replaces v1's ILD-centered mathematical formulation.

C1.justification: The central contribution shifts from ILD-based redundancy measurement and its correlation with rendering quality to a broader utility-based selection framework with theoretical analysis. The headline claim of matching full-data performance with 15% of frames and 75% of training time disappears, as does the proposed ILD-based pretraining quality predictor. IndoorTraj and reduced-data efficiency remain central.

C2.justification: v2 links coverage clustering to non-submodularity and DPP underperformance to non-monotonicity and numerical precision. It adds substantive applicability limits: coverage selection can excel below a 3% sampling ratio, while DPP can fail at 20% even with 64-bit precision. These explanations extend v1's redundancy and spatial-coverage interpretation.

D1.justification: v2 reports an authors' code-access URL and retains the principal hardware, CLIP, scaling, and kernel settings. Detailed ILD-stratified tuning-set construction is replaced by grid-search guidance. Explicit weights in the component-ablation table and the distinction between online and preloaded feature-extraction timing are removed.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning around DPP and submodular optimization, adding works such as Kulesza, Nemhauser, and Lin–Bilmes. It also expands SLAM, ray-sampling, and warping-consistency coverage while removing ILD-specific references. Prior view-selection heuristics are newly positioned as lacking theoretical grounding, beyond bibliographic or citation-style changes.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. The method narrative is reorganized into Preliminary and Utility Function Design sections, appendix contents are substantially replaced, and timing discussion moves to an appendix. Terminology changes include similarity to distance and ImgSim to DistSem.

P2.justification: The document changes from two columns to one. Comparison displays expand for DPP and real-world results; sampling-ratio plots become a larger 2-by-2 arrangement, and new heatmaps replace the correlation display. The opening convergence figure, joint resource-efficiency plot, and full-metric tables disappear, while dataset illustrations are retained and reformatted.

improvement.justification: Real-world testing, expanded utility comparisons, and code-access information strengthen v2. However, it removes perceptual-metric and joint resource-efficiency evidence and no longer separates feature-extraction costs in timing. Moreover, Equation (6) does not establish an order-independent set function, leaving the new submodularity claim in Proposition 2 unsupported. These material gains and weaknesses prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
